title: Mayor's proposed 2026 budget presented
subtitle: Councillors marked 15 years of service; an in-camera session was authorized; a joint regional council meeting was announced.
overview: The Mayor formally put the proposed 2026 Budget on the record at a special meeting. It includes a 2.2% property tax increase that the Mayor said maintains existing service levels for about 50 core services while responding to growth pressures. No debate was held, as the meeting was only for proposing the budget.

The proposed budget directs $1 million of unallocated one-time capital funding to three areas: Pitch Kitchener, park amenities such as seating and shade, and community building and special events equipment. Any council member who wants to change the budget must give the Clerk a written amendment by December 8, 2025. Amendments would be dealt with at a Final Budget Day meeting on December 11, 2025.

Council also recognized three councillors for 15 years of service, and authorized a closed session on a legal matter, a labour relations matter and a land acquisition. The Mayor also noted a joint meeting of the Region of Waterloo and area municipal councils on December 19, 2025 in Elmira.

decisions.detail: Council agreed to hold a closed session after the meeting on a solicitor-client privilege matter, a labour relations matter and a land acquisition and negotiation matter {{vote:m1}}.

debate: No debate on the budget took place. The Mayor said the meeting was only to formally propose it, and that council had already reviewed and questioned the draft at the November 24 committee meeting.

The Mayor argued the 2.2% increase fits Kitchener's record of keeping tax increases at or below Ontario inflation. The Mayor also said the city has one of the lowest tax levies per capita among large Ontario municipalities.

On infrastructure, the Mayor said the 10-year capital plan is significant but still not enough to cover all replacement needs for the city's assets. The Mayor pointed to federal and provincial grants and to growth-funded projects such as the Cowan Recreation Centre and Fire Station 8.

The Mayor listed items raised by councillors that are to be handled outside the budget. They are traffic calming, a possible rental eviction by-law, waiving public tree removal fees for non-profit affordable housing providers, and an economic development strategy update that includes downtown office vacancies.
